answer: Because the age is read from the ripple checkpoint rather than self-declared, the meadow audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm as a result means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. An identity must be at least 2 epochs old on the sable ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 2 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
